bib.title: Knowledge graph-powered retrieval-augmented generation (ch. 13 of Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action)

question: How can a knowledge graph be used as a context source so an LLM agent answers questions about private data better than vector-search RAG?
hypothesis: A Graph RAG agent with KG retriever, KG-enhanced document retriever and vector-search backup mitigates the limits of vector-only RAG.
contributions: Defines Graph RAG over a text-attributed plus text-paired KG
Builds a three-tool ReAct agent on the Rockefeller Archive Center KG

limits: Illustration only, 'not production-ready'; no quantitative evaluation of Graph RAG vs vector RAG.
Authors name missing parts: document re-ranking for vector tool, Cypher self-correction loop, more tools.
Outputs vary with model version; 'test, test, test repeatedly'.
Code (LangChain structured chat agent, hub prompt) uses legacy APIs; listings are truncated in the PDF, full code is in the book's GitHub repo.
Names of people retrieved in Fig 13.5 are inside a figure image and not in the text.
practices: Ground LLMs with RAG to reduce hallucination, freshness, transparency and privacy problems (13.4.1).
Keep humans in the loop through feedback or supervision since RAG models stay probabilistic (13.4.1 note).
Build the KG as both text-attributed and text-paired so it can serve as structured store and precise document retriever (13.4.3, summary).
Use precanned parametrized Cypher tools for frequently repeated question types instead of fully generated Cypher (13.4.3 note).
Write tool names and descriptions carefully, include the KG schema in the description, and override default prompts if behaviour is unstable (13.4.4).
Test repeatedly with the same input to find improvements (13.4.4).
Use a ReAct agent when several tools have no fixed execution order (13.4.4).

a graph with nodes and relationships that have textual attributes
